_note: Our own writing. Line pools for dialogue scenes: '@pool' in a scene picks one (never the same twice in a row). 'pool_<personality>' lines are added for NPCs with that personality; 'pool_friendly' lines are added at Friendly standing or better; 'pool_hostile' lines replace the pool at Wary or worse. Placeholders: see src/story/story_text.gd. '<pool>_<culture kit>' lines are added at hubs of that kit.

describe_npc: {npc_title} {npc} looks up as you approach, and {npc_quirk}.
This is {npc}, {npc_title} for {npc_faction}. First impression: someone who {npc_quirk}.
You'd guess {npc} has been {npc_role_lower} here a long time. The kind of person who {npc_quirk}.
greet_company_rep: {npc}, {npc_faction}. You're the new lancers? Good. Let's talk about what your license gets you.
Welcome to {hub}. {npc_faction} keeps an office here for pilots like you.
Callsign {callsign}, isn't it? I've read your file. Short file.
If it's licensed, I can get it printed. If it isn't, we can talk about how you get there.
{npc_faction} looks after the pilots who look after {npc_faction}. That's the arrangement.
Take a seat. Coffee's terrible, but it's hot.
greet_company_rep_gruff: Make it quick, pilot. I've got forty requisitions and one working printer.
You want something. Everybody wants something.
greet_company_rep_cheerful: There they are! Our favorite new pilots! Sit, sit.
Oh, perfect timing. I was just thinking about you lot.
greet_company_rep_formal: Good day. {npc}, {npc_title}. How may {npc_faction} assist you?
Please. State your business and I'll see what the contract allows.
greet_company_rep_friendly: {callsign}! Good work out there. People upstairs noticed.
My favorite customers. What do you need?
greet_company_rep_hostile: You've got some nerve coming back here after the last job.
{npc_faction} remembers, pilot. Say what you need and go.
I'm only talking to you because the contract says I have to.
greet_quartermaster: Printer's warm. Gear's on the racks. What do you need, pilot?
Sign here, here and here. No, I don't care what it says either.
Everything you're licensed for, I can print. Everything else, don't ask.
You break it, the printer makes you a new one. That's the beauty of it.
Kit check? Good. Most pilots forget until they're bleeding.
greet_quartermaster_gruff: Don't touch the printer. Tell me what you want and I'll touch the printer.
greet_quartermaster_weary: Third shift in a row. Go on, what is it.
Sure. Why not. Everyone else has asked for something today.
greet_quartermaster_friendly: Saved you the good hardsuit. Don't tell anyone.
For you lot? Anything that's on the license.
greet_quartermaster_hostile: Requisition form. In triplicate. Then we'll talk.
I heard what you did. Gear's on the racks. Help yourself, and be quick.
greet_bartender: Pilots drink half price. Kidding. Nobody pays here anyway, it's all on the ledger.
You look like you need one.
First one's for showing up alive.
If you're here for gossip, you'll have to drink something first.
greet_bartender_warm: Come in, come in. Out of the dust.
There's a stool with your name on it. Not literally. Well, once, but we sanded it off.
greet_bartender_sly: I hear things. You buy a drink, maybe you hear things too.
Everybody talks at my bar. Sooner or later.
greet_bartender_friendly: Your table's free. I kept it free.
greet_bartender_hostile: One drink. Then you find somewhere else to be.
Last time you lot were in, I lost three chairs.
greet_fixer: Looking for something? Everything's for sale, if the price is right.
Manna, favors, who owes who: I deal in all of it. Mostly the last two.
I don't ask where things come from. Don't ask where they go.
You've got the look of someone who needs a thing they can't print.
Talk quiet. The walls in {hub} have ears, and most of them are mine.
greet_fixer_sly: Well, well. Lancers. Let's see what you're worth.
I knew you'd come by. People always do.
greet_fixer_nervous: You weren't followed? Tell me you weren't followed.
greet_fixer_hostile: You owe me, and you know it.
I don't deal with people who burn their contacts.
greet_faction_agent: {npc}, {npc_faction}. We've been watching your squad. In a good way, mostly.
{npc_faction} has interests in this region. Interests that could use a few mechs.
Sit. I'll get straight to it: we have work, if you want it.
You're the ones {hub} won't stop talking about.
Lancers. Good. I was told to find lancers.
greet_faction_agent_formal: On behalf of {npc_faction}, thank you for meeting with me.
Please, be seated. This conversation is, of course, confidential.
greet_faction_agent_zealous: {npc_faction} is the only future this world has. Will you help build it?
Every day we wait, people suffer. Are you ready to act?
greet_faction_agent_friendly: Our friends return. {npc_faction} doesn't forget its friends.
Good to see you, {callsign}. I've kept something back for you.
greet_faction_agent_hostile: You have a lot of explaining to do.
{npc_faction} is not pleased with your squad, pilot.
Give me one reason not to report you.
greet_local: Oh! You're one of the pilots. From the big machines.
Morning. Or whatever it is. The sun's been weird all week.
You're not from around here. Nobody walks like that around here.
Are you here to help, or just passing through?
Careful on the main road. Potholes big enough to lose a boot.
Hello. Sorry. I don't talk to many pilots.
greet_local_nervous: Please don't let the big machines step on the well again.
greet_local_warm: Welcome! Have you eaten? You look like you haven't eaten.
Ah, a new face. Sit with me a while.
greet_local_weary: If you're here to tell us to evacuate again, we're not going.
greet_local_friendly: It's you! Everyone's talking about what you did.
My kids have been playing 'lancers' all week. You're very popular.
greet_local_hostile: You've done enough. Leave us be.
My cousin's farm was under that fight of yours.
We don't want your kind here.
greet_mechanic: Mind the coolant, it eats boots.
Your frame's tougher than it looks. It's also dirtier than it looks.
If you've come to complain about the actuators, join the queue.
Hand me that spanner. No, the other spanner. Thanks. What do you want?
Printer makes the parts. I make them work together.
greet_mechanic_cheerful: Oh, I love your mech. Can I take the leg apart? Just a little?
Hey! Come look at this, it's beautiful. It's a valve.
greet_mechanic_hostile: You wrecked it, you fix it.
My bay, my rules. You're not on my list.
menu_prompt: So. What can I do for you?
Still here? Good. What is it?
farewell_friendly: Take care of yourself, {callsign}. I mean it.
Anytime. You know where I am.
rumor: They say something big crashed out past {place} last month. Nobody who went to look came back.
{hub_faction} is pulling people off the perimeter. Nobody knows why.
There's a freighter captain in the docks selling 'medical supplies'. They're not medical supplies.
Someone's been buying up every water filter in {hub}. Every single one.
Old-timers say the mines out east go deeper than anyone mapped.
A courier came in yesterday, babbling about mechs with no pilots, walking in a line.
The administrator has a second office no one's allowed in.
The weather sats keep going dark over the same valley.
My sister says {npc_faction} is about to sign something big. Big enough to change who runs this place.
There's a bounty on a pilot callsigned 'Lantern'. Nobody's ever seen them.
Raiders have been hitting {place}. They're getting bolder.
Half the farms on the north side haven't paid their water share. Something's coming to a head.
license_explain: Manna won't buy you a frame, pilot. Your License Level is what you've earned: every mission you finish, win or lose, it goes up by one. Each level gives you a license rank to spend on one of a manufacturer's frame licenses; rank I opens some of its gear, rank II the frame itself, rank III the best parts. Until then, it's GMS: the Everest and the standard gear, which every pilot is licensed for.

Licenses are the currency that matters. You don't buy a frame, you're licensed for it. Finish a mission and you go up a License Level; spend that level's license rank with a manufacturer and their gear opens up, rank by rank. Once you're licensed for something, you never lose it.

You want a new mech? Fly missions. After each one your License Level goes up and you get a license rank to put toward a manufacturer: IPS-Northstar, Smith-Shimano, HORUS, Harrison Armory. Ranks are bought in order, I, II, III; at rank II of a frame's license you can fly that frame, and the gear from every rank you hold mixes freely between your mechs. Until then, GMS has you covered.
printing_explain: Anything you're licensed for, the printer can make. Your mech gets wrecked, we print a new one when you've got ten hours and somewhere safe: that's a full repair. But you can only have one mech printed at a time. Print a new one and the old one stops working.
Printers are everywhere Union is. Give me ten quiet hours and the licenses, and you'll walk out with a mech fresh off the line. Gear too. What I can't print is something you're not licensed for.
gear_explain: Pilot gear isn't licensed. Take what you need: one set of armor, up to two weapons, up to three other pieces. That's the limit for a mission, because that's what you can actually carry.
Armor, two weapons, three other bits of kit. More than that and you're a pack mule, not a pilot.
Carry what keeps you alive: armor, two weapons, three more bits. That's the rule.
Kit limit's simple: one armor, two guns, three gadgets. Choose well.
reserves_explain: Reserves are whatever extra you bring to the next mission: spare repairs, a favor, a map, a ride out. They last one mission. Use them or lose them.
Think of reserves as an edge for the next job. Some help your mech, some help the story: a keycard, a contact, a distraction. After the mission, they're gone.
rep_favor_intro: If you're in good with {npc_faction}, I can make a call. Repairs, rented gear, maybe even a spare battery. No promises.
I could put in a word. It'll cost you a favor down the line, probably.
Let me see what the account will stand.
drink_offer: Something to take the edge off? Or are you here to make friends?
barter_intro: Name what you're after. I'll tell you what it'll cost. Sometimes manna, usually a favor.
Everything's got a price. Even here. Especially here.
You want it, I can find it. Maybe.
I might have something for you. Might.
What are you buying with, pilot? Favors? Secrets?
agent_job_intro: We have a job. It's not pleasant, but it matters.
{npc_faction} needs something done, and your squad is close.
There's work. Paid in favors, as always.
There's always work for people like you.
My employer has needs. You have skills.
local_want_line: If you really want to help... {npc_want}. That's what we need.
mechanic_creative: Want to build something? Bring me an idea and some time, and we'll see.
Bay three's free if you want to tinker. Don't weld anything to the ceiling again.
I've got tools, you've got ideas. Let's make something.
Grab a wrench or get out of the way.
check_success: Huh. Didn't think you had it in you.
check_fail: You'll have to do better than that.
briefing_close: Get your reserves in order. You deploy soon.
Gear up. We go when you're ready.
Boots on the ground in a few hours.
Briefing's over. Go check your mechs.
debrief_victory: It's done. Good work, all of you.
We got it done. {hub} owes you.
You came through. I'll remember that.
Solid work. That's the job done.
You did what you were asked, and then some.
debrief_defeat: We lost that one. It's not the end, but it hurts.
Not every mission goes our way. We regroup.
That went badly. We'll have to live with it.
Get some rest. We'll talk about what went wrong.
We'll recover from this. We have to.
Not our day. We learn and go again.
debrief_draw: Neither side got what it wanted. That's something, I suppose.
A stalemate. We live to try again.
debrief_level: Whatever happened out there, you learned from it. Every pilot's License Level goes up after a mission, win or lose.
You're all a License Level higher now. That means new triggers, talents and license ranks. Spend them well.
Every one of you comes out of this a License Level higher. That's how it works, good day or bad.
Level up, pilots. New license rank, new trigger, new talent. You earned them out there.
Whatever the result, you're better pilots than you were this morning. One more License Level each.
supplies_explain: Everyday food, water and a bunk come with the job; nobody counts rations for you. What you plan for is the extra: kit for crossing hostile ground, spare repair materials for your mech, and what you carry yourself.

The printer covers the basics. For a mission you want more: Supplies for bad ground, repair stock for the mech (that's two more repairs in the field), and your own kit: rations, a survival kit, patches.
You carry what you can carry: armor, two weapons, three bits of kit. Rations and a survival kit count. Anything bigger, you bring as reserves: get it through a contact, or go scrounging.
supplies_how: Two ways to get it before you deploy: I can put in a word if you're in good standing (that's calling in a favor), or you go dig it up yourself at the market. Either way it's your downtime.
Ask me nicely and I'll requisition it, if your standing holds up. Or hit the salvage yards and barter. Pick one: you've only got so much downtime.
deal_offer: Tell you what. Help me with {npc_want}, and I'll see you get {npc_deal_reward} for your next drop.
There is something: {npc_want}. Do that, and {npc_deal_reward} is yours for the next mission.
A trade, then. You handle {npc_want}; I come through with {npc_deal_reward}.
deal_waiting: The job's on the board. Do it, and we're square.
Still waiting on that job, pilot.
You know where to find the work. I'll keep my end ready.
The deal stands. The job's still open.
We have an arrangement. I'm waiting on your end.
deal_thanks: You came through. Here's my end, as promised.
Job done, and I don't forget. Take it.
That's a debt paid. Good work.
deal_off: The job went bad, so the deal's off. If you want something from me now, you'll have to find another way.
That didn't work out. No hard feelings, but the offer's gone. Come back when you've got something else.
secret_revealed: You read it in the way they hold themselves: {npc_secret}
They don't say it, but you're sure of it now: {npc_secret}
journey_start: Getting to {place} means crossing hostile ground.
Between {hub} and {place} is a long stretch of country nobody would cross for fun.
The route to {place} is bad: broken ground, no cover, nothing friendly.
journey_supplied: You brought the right kit. The crossing is long and dull, which is exactly what you wanted.
Your supplies get the squad across without trouble.
journey_ok: You make it across, tired but in one piece.
A hard crossing, but nobody's hurt and nothing's lost.
journey_bad: The crossing takes everything you had. You arrive spent, battered and late.
It goes badly: a rockslide, a wrong turn, a long cold night. You get there, barely.
debrief_twist: Looking back, nothing was what the briefing said. {twist_reveal}
greet_company_rep_old_west: Howdy, pilots. Company office is open, but the coffee's from Tuesday.
You'll be the new lancers. Wipe your boots.
greet_quartermaster_old_west: Printer's out back in the old freight shed. Mind the tumbleweeds.
Ammo, armor, rations. Sign the ledger, partner.
greet_bartender_old_west: Sit down, dust off. First one's on the house, second one's on your tab.
Pilots in my saloon again. Keep the mechs off the hitching rail.
greet_fixer_old_west: Lookin' for something the general store don't carry?
Everything out here's for trade. Even me, for the right favor.
greet_faction_agent_old_west: The railroad's got work, and the railroad doesn't take no for an answer.
Marshal's office could use some iron on its side.
greet_local_old_west: Howdy. You're the ones with the big walkers.
Mind your step. Snakes this time of year, and worse.
greet_mechanic_old_west: Dust gets in everything. Your actuators too.
Bring her in, I'll get the grit out of her joints.
rumor_old_west: Somebody's been jumping claims out by {place}. Leaves no tracks.
The rail company bought the water rights. Nobody voted on it.
Ghost lights on the mesa again. The old-timers won't ride out after dark.
There's a bounty posted on the general store door. No name, just a mech's paint job.
greet_company_rep_medieval_tech: Well met, lancers. The house recognizes your license, if not your manners.
Approach. The steward has told me of you.
greet_quartermaster_medieval_tech: The armoury is open to licensed pilots. Touch nothing with a crest on it.
Your kit, as the steward ordered. And a ration of bread, by custom.
greet_bartender_medieval_tech: Welcome to the inn, travelers. Mind the hounds.
Ale or wine? We've no fancier drink, and no fancier guests usually.
greet_fixer_medieval_tech: Not here. The Baron's men drink at that table. Follow me.
You'll find nothing for sale on the Market Cross that I can't find for you cheaper.
greet_faction_agent_medieval_tech: My lord has need of lancers. Kneel, if it pleases you. It would please him.
The house remembers those who serve it. And those who do not.
greet_local_medieval_tech: Begging your pardon. Are you knights?
You came through the gate in those machines? The whole town's talking.
greet_mechanic_medieval_tech: Steel and servos, same as any forge. Bring it here.
The castle smiths can't fix what you've got. I can.
rumor_medieval_tech: The old baron's heir hasn't been seen at court in a month.
They say the river bridge was built by the first settlers, and something's buried under it.
There'll be a tourney at midsummer. Lancers too, this year.
The serfs on the east fields have stopped paying the grain tax.
greet_company_rep_cyberpunk: You're on the visitor roster. Badge stays visible at all times.
Lancers. Good. My quarterly targets thank you.
greet_quartermaster_cyberpunk: Kit's on the rack, feed's on the screen, rain's on everything.
Printer queue's long. I can bump you, if your standing's good.
greet_bartender_cyberpunk: Sit. The noise keeps the drones from listening.
What are you drinking? And who sent you?
greet_fixer_cyberpunk: Off the grid or on it? Pick fast, I've got three other calls.
I can get you anything. Nothing comes clean.
greet_faction_agent_cyberpunk: My employer would prefer this meeting never happened.
You've got a clean record. Let's see how long it stays clean.
greet_local_cyberpunk: Don't look up at the ads. They look back.
You lost? Nobody comes this low on purpose.
greet_mechanic_cyberpunk: Pull it into the chop shop. No questions, no receipts.
Rain gets in the seals. Let me look.
rumor_cyberpunk: Somebody wiped a whole floor of the Archive Tower last night. No alarms.
The undercity lost power again. Third time this week. Corporate says it's maintenance.
There's a street doc on Level Nine who can fix anything, for a favor.
The ads went quiet for one minute at midnight. Everyone saw the same face.
greet_company_rep_retrofuturistic: Welcome, welcome! The future is here, and it's licensed!
Pilots! Just like the posters. Come in, come in.
greet_quartermaster_retrofuturistic: Ration packs, chrome-plated. Don't ask me why.
Everything you need for tomorrow, today!
greet_bartender_retrofuturistic: Malt, float or something stronger? The jukebox only plays one song.
Pull up a stool, the robot will take your order. Eventually.
greet_fixer_retrofuturistic: Psst. Prototype parts, straight off the line.
The world's fair left a lot behind. I collect it.
greet_faction_agent_retrofuturistic: The Bureau of Tomorrow has a proposal for you.
greet_local_retrofuturistic: Are you from the future too? Everyone here says they are.
My granddad built that monorail. Nobody remembers how it works.
greet_mechanic_retrofuturistic: Tubes, coils and tail fins. Your rig'll look swell.
Atomic age tech, new age problems. What's broken?
rumor_retrofuturistic: The weather-control dome hasn't worked in years. Someone's been fixing it at night.
The monorail runs one extra car after midnight. Nobody gets on.
The old rocket at the fairground is fueled. Someone checked.
They're tearing down the Civic Dome. Half the town's protesting.
greet_company_rep_east_asian: Welcome. Please, sit. Business is better over tea.
Your arrival was expected. The prefecture extends its courtesy.
greet_quartermaster_east_asian: Your kit is ready. It has been blessed, by custom. It doesn't hurt.
Rations, rope, rain capes. The terraces are steep.
greet_bartender_east_asian: Lanterns are lit, kettle is on. Sit wherever there's a cushion.
greet_fixer_east_asian: Not in the market. In the alley behind the lantern seller.
What you want can be found. What you owe will be remembered.
greet_faction_agent_east_asian: The clan elders asked for you by name. That is an honor, and a warning.
My prefect values discretion above all.
greet_local_east_asian: Mind the steps, they're older than the town.
Are you here for the festival? Or for the trouble?
greet_mechanic_east_asian: The gantry temple has fixed mechs for two hundred years.
Bring it under the gate. We'll see what it needs.
rumor_east_asian: The shrine bell rang on its own three nights ago.
The upper terraces have been bought by someone nobody's met.
The ferry pilots won't cross the lake after dark anymore.
The festival is in a week. Someone wants it cancelled.
farewell_east_asian: May the lanterns guide you home.
greet_company_rep_union_core: Your credentials check out. Welcome to the core, pilots.
Everything here runs to schedule. Please don't change that.
greet_quartermaster_union_core: Standard issue, quality assured. Anything you need is a request away.
Your allocation's been prepared. You won't find the frontier's shortages here.
greet_bartender_union_core: Welcome to the commons. Everything's on the house: it's always on the house here.
Long way from the frontier, aren't you?
greet_fixer_union_core: You'd be surprised what the core wants that it can't officially have.
Even utopia has a back door.
greet_faction_agent_union_core: The Committee has an interest in your squad's work.
Union thanks you for your service. Now, about the next one.
greet_local_union_core: You've been out there? What's it actually like?
We see the frontier on the omninet. It looks so far away.
greet_mechanic_union_core: Clean bay, clean tools, clean work.
Your mech's seen some real dirt. I'll treat it gently.
rumor_union_core: There's a delegation leaving for a world nobody's heard of.
A committee seat has been empty for a month. Nobody will say why.
The orbital elevator closed for 'maintenance' twice this week.
Someone in the archives is asking about old colony records.
greet_local_frontier_colony: Welcome to the colony. Population: not enough.
You're the first new faces since the last supply drop.
rumor_frontier_colony: The water recycler's been making a new noise.
Half the colony charter expires next year. Nobody knows what happens then.
farewell_frontier_colony: Come back when you can. We could use you.
greet_instructor: Rookie. Good to see you on your feet.
There's my new squad. Questions? I've got time.
Back from the range in one piece. That's the first lesson.
At ease. What do you need?
downtime_intro: The squad has a few days at {hub} before the next job. Time to rest, repair, and see who owes who.
Downtime at {hub}. The mechs go into the printer bay for a full repair; the pilots go looking for whatever they need.
A breather at {hub}. Ten hours in a bunk, a fresh print of every mech, and a little time to call your own.
dt_buy_some_time_low: {callsign} stalls as hard as they can, but it only buys a little time, and only by doing something drastic.
{callsign}'s delay works, barely. Whatever's coming is still coming soon.
dt_buy_some_time_mid: {callsign} buys enough time, but it's getting precarious.
{callsign} keeps things from boiling over. For now. It won't hold forever.
dt_buy_some_time_high: {callsign} buys all the time the squad needs.
Whatever was coming, {callsign} has pushed it well past the next mission.
dt_gather_information_low: {callsign} digs too deep looking into {topic}, and has to choose between the answer and a clean getaway.
{callsign}'s questions about {topic} get noticed by the wrong people.
dt_gather_information_mid: {callsign} finds out about {topic}, but leaves a mess behind.
{callsign} gets answers about {topic}. Someone will want something for them.
dt_gather_information_high: {callsign} comes back knowing everything worth knowing about {topic}.
Nobody even noticed {callsign} asking about {topic}, and the answers are good.
dt_get_a_damn_drink_low: {callsign} wakes up somewhere unfamiliar, with a headache and a very patchy memory.
Nobody's sure what happened to {callsign} last night. Least of all {callsign}.
{callsign} says too much to the wrong person over drinks.
{callsign}'s night out ends with a broken chair and an apology to make.
dt_get_a_damn_drink_mid: {callsign} has a night to remember: something gained, something lost.
{callsign} makes a friend, a scene, and a mistake, not necessarily in that order.
dt_get_a_damn_drink_high: {callsign} has the best night anyone's had at {hub} in years, and walks out ahead.
Drinks with {callsign} turn into stories people will tell for a while.
dt_get_connected_low: {callsign}'s contact will help, but only if the favor gets done right now.
{subject} can help {callsign}, but wants something first.
dt_get_connected_mid: {subject} comes through for {callsign}. There'll be a favor to repay.
{callsign} gets the help, and a debt to go with it.
dt_get_creative_low: {callsign} stares at the workbench for days. Nothing.
dt_get_creative_mid: {callsign} makes real progress on {subject}. It needs a little more to be done.
{subject} is half-built on {callsign}'s bench, and looking promising.
dt_get_focused: Hours of practice. {callsign} is better at {subject} now.
dt_get_organized: {callsign} puts people together around an idea: {subject}.
dt_power_at_a_cost: {callsign} gets {subject}. The price is still to be paid.
{subject}: done. {callsign} knew it would cost something.
dt_scrounge_and_barter_low: {callsign} comes back with {subject}, and a problem.
dt_scrounge_and_barter_mid: {callsign} gets {subject}, and pays for it one way or another.
{subject}, acquired. {callsign} won't say what it cost.
downtime_recap_header: What the squad did with the time:
arc_after_win: Last time went your way, and {b} noticed.
{b} lost ground last time. They won't let it happen twice.
You won the last round against {b}. Word travels.
arc_after_loss: Last time cost you, and {b} smells blood.
{b} came out ahead last time. Now they're bolder.
The last job against {b} went badly. This one has to count.
briefing_callback: Word about "{last_title}" got around: {last_outcome_line}. People here remember.
Last time, at {last_place}, {last_outcome_line}. This one's different.
You all know how "{last_title}" turned out: {last_outcome_line}. Now, the next job.
debrief_fallen: Before anything else: {fallen} didn't come back. We remember them.
We lost {fallen} out there. Nothing about this job was worth that.
background_ack: Huh. You know what you're talking about.
Not many pilots would say that. Thank you.
debrief_cascade: {cascade} had an NHP cascade out there. You got it shut down. Have it cycled before it flies again.
I read the logs: {cascade}'s NHP slipped its shackles mid-fight. That doesn't go in a report lightly.
{cascade}'s NHP cascaded. You all walked away from it, which is more than some squads can say.
